title: geo-routing-kms-consent-orchestrator-and-audit-clarity
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Adds jurisdiction-aware routing for KMS requests, a consent coordinator service for cross-region key usage, RBAC v2 policy templates for region-scoped operator bindings, and audit header normalizers. Backwards-compatible; requires config toggles for rollout.
description: [Summary] Add a small orchestration layer (kms-consent-coordinator) and accompanying RBAC v2 policy templates to enforce per-tenant region pinning for KMS usage, plus an audit header clarity sanitizer to make residency decisions auditable and debuggable. | [Motivation] Customers running Private and Dedicated deployments require deterministic behavior when tenant traffic needs to be pinned to a geographic jurisdiction (data residency) while allowing safe fallbacks to alternate KMS providers when consent is present. Previously, routing logic and KMS consent checks were scattered across services and produced noisy audit entries; this PR centralizes consent negotiation, makes routing deterministic, and produces a compact, signed audit envelope. | [What changed] 1) services/kms-consent-coordinator/: new lightweight HTTP service that performs a deterministic consent handshake between operator claims, tenant residency profile, and available KMS providers. Exposes /v1/consent-check and /v1/tokenize endpoints. 2) pkg/authorizer/policy_templates/region_scoped_bindings.go: new RBAC v2 templates to create operator-scoped, region-bound role bindings with TTL and audit annotations. 3) audit/proxy/clarity_sanitizer.go: middleware that canonicalizes residency headers (X-Resident-Region, X-KMS-Origin) and emits an audit envelope field audit.residency_hint for downstream indexing. 4) tools/migrate_region_bindings.py: migration helper to translate legacy tenancy labels into new RBAC templates. 5) integration/region_routing_e2e.test: new e2e harness that simulates multi-KMS environments and asserts deterministic routing and audit envelope contents. 6) docs/ops/kms-region-consent.md: operational runbook and feature flags for staged rollout. | [Commits] - Add kms-consent-coordinator service and tests - Implement region-scoped RBAC templates and migration script - Add audit clarity sanitizer and telemetry - Wire-up integration tests and CI job - Fix linting and type issues reported by reviewers | [Files of interest] services/kms-consent-coordinator/server.go, services/kms-consent-coordinator/consent_handler.go, pkg/authorizer/policy_templates/region_scoped_bindings.go, audit/proxy/clarity_sanitizer.go, integration/region_routing_e2e.test, tools/migrate_region_bindings.py, docs/ops/kms-region-consent.md | [Testing] Unit tests for policy template generation and consent coordinator logic; integration test running against a two-KMS local harness (mock-AWS-KMS, mock-azure-kms). CI added a new matrix row (region-routing-e2e) which runs on a thin VM image; initial runs failed due to missing mock KMS certs, fixed by adding test fixtures. Performance: average consent-check latency is ~12ms under load in the e2e harness; the coordinator is async-friendly and supports piggybacking with existing tokenization flows. | [Security considerations] Consent coordinator signs consent decisions with a short-lived key and includes a stable nonce to prevent replay. RBAC templates include explicit audit annotations and deny-by-default semantics for operators outside tenant's geozone. KMS tokens are never stored by the coordinator; it only mediates proof-of-consent and issues ephemeral delegation handles. | [Compatibility and rollout] Feature gated under agent.config.region_pinning.enabled (default false). Migration script converts legacy labels to RBAC bindings; recommended staged rollout: enable audit_sanitizer in canary, run migrations as dry-run, enable coordinator in canary region, progressively flip flag. | [Review conversation highlights] - Luis Ortega: "Please add a unit test that verifies audit envelope contains 'residency_hint' for edge cases (tenant no-preference)." Author: "Added test and a comment explaining default fallback semantics." - Samir Patel: "Concern: how do we guarantee key origin attestation when we fallback to a secondary KMS?" Author: "Coordinator attaches a KMS-origin assertion and the proxy validates provider fingerprints; added docs and telemetry to track such fallbacks." - Mei Chen: "Lint errors in audit sanitizer and a potential nil deref in migration script." Author: "Fixed in commits 4 and 6; added extra checks and tightened types." - Security review (automated): flagged missing signature rotation for coordinator keys. Author: "Implemented rotation via existing kms/rotation library and added e2e coverage for rotated keys." | [CI and checks] - unit: pass - lint: initially failed (go vet/style), fixed - integration: pass (region-routing-e2e) - security-scan: pass after rotation fix | [Merge] Approved by reviewers on 2026-03-04, merged via squash by release-bot on 2026-03-05. Merge commit: "squash! geo-routing-kms-consent-orchestrator-and-audit-clarity — Priya Menon" | [Follow-ups] ENG-1302: add RBAC auditing dashboards to Console (linked), ENG-1310: load test coordinator under production traffic patterns. | [Notes] This PR is intentionally conservative about automatic KMS failover; operator override is required for non-consent fallback to preserve compliance guarantees.
